# S102 — startRun re-checks that the project is still registered

**Findings:**  · **Size:** S · **Tree:**

**Not in this slice:**

## Why

S38 reviewer note, accepted as a limit. A run planned before ork projects rm can still launch for the removed project, because startRun (internal/daemon/runs.go ~:403) does not re-check that the project is registered; the handlers.go comment on projects.rm says so. Together with S35 (removed-project runs stay visible) and S77 (queued runs of a removed project stop) this closes the gap.

## Files

- `internal/daemon/runs.go` (startRun ~:403): refuse with a clear error when the project is not in the registry (use the cached registry from S76 when the read fails).
- `internal/daemon/runs_test.go`: the test.
- `internal/daemon/handlers.go`: update the projects.rm comment.

## Failing tests

- TestStartRunRefusesAProjectRemovedAfterPlanning: a run planned, then its project removed, is refused at start with an error naming the project, with no worktree and no run record.
- TestStartRunStillWorksWithAUnreadableRegistryUsingTheCache (S76 behaviour is unchanged).

## Implement

1. Tests first. 2. In startRun look the project up (cache fallback) before creating anything. 3. Update the comment and docs/design.md if it describes the gap.
